summary: Reviewed the typed argument profile against the retained ASPIC section 3.3, Carneades Definition 10 and case-constructor preconditions. The implementation distinguishes explicit symbolic attack semantics from unverified source meaning and prevents graph acceptance from deleting candidates.
findings: Rebut cannot target a strict top inference; undercut targets an applicability proposition; premise attacks target named premises.
Defeat propagates to dependent arguments; cyclic support and resource limits remain unresolved.
Model proposed priorities cannot suppress an attack without separately accepted preference hashes; priorities must be acyclic.
Ordinary support, challenged assumptions and active exceptions have distinct consequences and questions.
Case operators require shared factors and retained quotations, preserve hypothetical labels and do not certify factual factor extraction or precedent authority.
This is a bounded local adaptation; ASPIC rationality theorems and full Carneades proof standards are not claimed.
